issue: far-tax-02 is not self-contained: its stem says 'Using the previous item' and omits the pretax income ($600,000), tax-exempt interest ($30,000) and fines ($12,000) needed to answer. Practice sets and review queues are shuffled, so the 'previous item' is usually not far-tax-01. It also shows far-tax-01's key ($111,720) as option (a) and in its explanation, so whichever order they appear in, one item gives away the other's answer.
evidence: src/lib/quiz.ts:84-86 shuffles the eligible items (shuffle(...).sort(by attempts), then shuffle(picked)), and mixed and mastery sets interleave modules (lines 95-98, 114-135). Seen on its own, far-tax-02 gives only the $50,000 depreciation difference, the 21% rate and no beginning balances, so total expense can't be computed. Recomputed with far-tax-01's facts: current (600,000 − 30,000 + 12,000 − 50,000) × 21% = 111,720, deferred 50,000 × 21% = 10,500, total 122,220. That's the key, but it can only be reached with facts from another item. Option (a) '$111,720 — That's only current tax' is far-tax-01's key.
source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ checks 3 and 6 (stem completeness; one item revealing the answer to another)
fix: Rewrite far-tax-02 to stand alone: 'Pretax book income is $600,000, including $30,000 of tax-exempt interest and $12,000 of nondeductible fines. Tax depreciation exceeds book depreciation by $50,000 (arising this year). The enacted rate is 21%, and there are no beginning deferred balances. What is total income tax expense?' To stop the two items cueing each other, change far-tax-02's numbers (e.g., pretax $700,000, so total = 21% × 682,000 = 143,220) or merge the pair into one two-part item.

issue: The journal scorer marks the lesson's own entry format wrong. The lesson's JE block records the provision with two expense lines ('Income tax expense — current' and 'Income tax expense — deferred'). The TBS keys accept only one combined 'Income tax expense' debit, and scoreJournal matches line by line, so a correct entry that splits expense into its current and deferred amounts loses 2 cells.
evidence: Lesson lines 99-107: Dr IT expense—current 159,600; Dr IT expense—deferred 6,300. r3 key: Dr Income tax expense 123,750 / Dr DTA 5,000 / Cr Income taxes payable 113,750 / Cr DTL 15,000. Simulated src/lib/tbsScoring.ts scoreJournal on the response Dr IT expense 113,750, Dr IT expense 10,000, Dr DTA 5,000, Cr ITP 113,750, Cr DTL 15,000 (balanced, 128,750 = 128,750). The expected 123,750 line finds no match (wrong); one IT-expense line is 'blamed' and the other becomes an 'Extra line' (wrong). Result: 3 of 5 cells (60%) for a correct entry. u10 works the same way: 286,650 + 23,100 split across two lines scores 3 of 5 (maxLines 5 allows it).
source: ASC 740-10-50-9 (current and deferred components of tax expense are separately disclosed, so separate lines are standard practice); src/lib/tbsScoring.ts scoreJournal
fix: Do one of the following. (a) Change the lesson's JE block to a single 'Income tax expense 165,900' debit and add a note: 'current 159,600 + deferred 6,300'. (b) Add the accounts 'Income tax expense — current' and 'Income tax expense — deferred' to both TBS account lists and key the split entry. (c) Change scoreJournal to sum same-account, same-side lines before matching. Option (c) fixes the problem for every JE TBS.

issue: These items are pure recall but are labeled skill 'analysis' and difficulty 3, two skill levels too high. far-tax-27 ('How are DTLs classified? All as noncurrent') is a near-copy of far-tax-07, which is correctly labeled remembering/1. far-tax-20 ('Is a DTL recognized on nondeductible goodwill? No') recalls a single scope exception.
evidence: far-tax-07: remembering/1. far-tax-27: analysis/3. The stems have 0.86 Jaccard similarity (cues.md), and the options (by related asset / all current / all noncurrent / by reversal date) are effectively the same. Both labels feed the FAR skill-mix targets (R&U 5-15%, App 45-55%, Analysis 35-45%; content/sections/far.yaml).
source: AICPA 2026 Blueprint skill definitions; content/sections/far.yaml skillAllocation
fix: Set skill 'remembering' and difficulty 1 on both items. Better still, replace far-tax-27 with a new item, since it duplicates far-tax-07 (see the redundancy finding).

issue: Labels are inflated by one level. Several one-step computations are labeled analysis/difficulty 3; far-tax-21 to -28 appear to have been batch-labeled. These are the simplest items in the module, so the easy-to-hard progression is inverted and the analysis share is overstated. far-tax-14 is recall labeled application. far-tax-06 asks only 'where' the effect is recognized, yet it carries calc: true.
evidence: Recomputed, every one is a single operation. 21: 30,000 × 25% = 7,500. 22: 30,000 × 21% = 6,300. 23: 40,000 × 25% = 10,000. 24: (200,000 − 10,000) × 25% = 47,500. 25: 47,500 + 5,000 = 52,500. 28: 80% × 90,000 = 72,000. x3-08: 950,000 × 21% = 199,500. chk2: read 200,000 from the stem. By contrast, far-tax-11 (50,000 × 21%) is labeled application/1 and far-tax-01 (four adjustments) application/2. Practice and exam pool labels as they stand: application 15, remembering 4, analysis 14 (42%). Corrected (with finding 003): remembering 7 (21%), application 21 (64%), analysis 5 (15%). That is well outside FAR's 35-45% analysis target. far-tax-06's answer needs no number; the 32,000 appears only in the explanation.
source: AICPA 2026 Blueprint skill definitions; content/sections/far.yaml skillAllocation
fix: Relabel 21, 22, 23, 24, 25 and 28 as application, difficulty 1 (22 may be 2). Relabel x3-08 as application/1 and chk2 as application. Relabel far-tax-14 as remembering/1. Remove calc from far-tax-06 (or set it false). Then add genuine analysis items (see the coverage finding) so the module's analysis share is real.

issue: Some distractor rationales and trap labels do not describe the error that produces the number. Four distractors say only 'Not the computation.' (trap 'distractor-number'), although each comes from a specific misconception, and one cannot be produced by any plausible error. Other trap labels name the wrong misconception.
evidence: Each distractor reproduced from its stem in python. 21(c) 22,500 = 30,000 × (1 − 25%): an after-tax or net amount; rationale 'Not the computation.' 22(c) 9,000 = 30,000 × 30%: no 30% rate appears anywhere in the stem, so no plausible error yields it (the plausible errors give 7,500 at the current rate, 1,200 for the rate change only, or 13,800 with both rates applied). 24(b) 52,500 = (200,000 + 10,000) × 25%: adds the muni interest, a wrong-sign error; rationale 'Not the computation.' 24(c) 2,500 = 10,000 × 25%: the tax effect of the muni alone (partial-computation), but trap is 'reversed'. 28(c) 80,000 = 80% × 100,000: applies the 80% to the NOL rather than to taxable income; rationale 'Not the computation.' 19(d) 74,000 = 0.3×100,000 + 0.3×80,000 + 0.4×50,000, the expected value: a wrong-rule (wrong measurement method) error, but trap is 'wrong-classification'. 08(a) 1,000,000: recognizing the full position (all-or-nothing) is a wrong-rule error, not 'partial-computation'. x3-06(a) 63,000 = 300,000 × 21%: rationale says 'Applies the current 21% rate', but the stem states no current rate; 21% is the Year 2 enacted rate.
source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ check 2 (trap label matches the misconception)
fix: Rewrite the rationales and traps. 21(c): 'This is the difference net of tax (30,000 × 75%); the DTL is the tax effect, 30,000 × 25%', trap partial-computation. 22(c): replace 9,000 with 1,200 ('only the 4-point rate change') or 13,800, with a matching rationale. 24(b): 'Adds the muni interest instead of subtracting it: 210,000 × 25%', trap wrong-sign. 24(c): trap partial-computation. 28(c): 'Applies 80% to the NOL instead of to taxable income', trap wrong-rule. 19(d): trap wrong-rule. 08(a): trap wrong-rule. x3-06(a): 'Applies the Year 2 rate (21%) to the whole difference'.

issue: Answer cues. In chk1 and 03 the key is by far the longest option, and the only one hedged as a complete rule. far-tax-20's key is the 2-character 'No', and distractor (c) 'Yes, as a DTA' contradicts its own stem, which asks about a DTL. In far-x3-26 the only absolutes ('Only when', 'Never ... always') sit in the distractors. far-tax-25's stem gives far-tax-24's key ($47,500 current tax).
evidence: Option lengths in characters: chk1 key 59 vs 34-41 for the distractors; 03 key 63 vs 28-45, with 'always' only in distractor (a); 20 key 2 vs 13-24. x3-26: (b) 'Only when ... remote', (d) 'Never; ... always'. far-tax-24's key (d) is $47,500; far-tax-25 opens 'Current tax expense is $47,500 ...'. Sessions are shuffled, so 25 often comes before 24.
fix: chk1: shorten the key to 'Warranty costs accrued before they are deductible', or lengthen the distractors to match. 03: give each option a parallel full clause (e.g., 'The rate in effect when the difference originated'; 'The enacted rate for the reversal year'), and drop 'always'. 20: rewrite the options as parallel statements ('No DTL; the excess of book goodwill over tax basis is an exception' / 'A DTL at the enacted rate' / 'A DTL only when goodwill is impaired' / 'A DTL measured at the effective rate'), or retire the item (see the scope finding). x3-26: give one distractor a qualifier and soften the others ('When realization is probable but not certain'). 25: change its current tax to a figure unrelated to far-tax-24 (e.g., $61,000).

issue: The key 'Either way, by policy' is vague, and the distractor pair frames it. 'Either way' refers to the other options, and the only alternative they offer is 'operating expense'. ASC 740-10-45-25 permits interest as income taxes or interest expense, and penalties as income taxes or another expense classification. Interest expense is usually nonoperating. The two 'Only ...' distractors also signal that the hedged option is the key.
evidence: Options: (a) 'Only as income tax expense', (b) 'Either way, by policy', (c) 'Only as operating expense', (d) 'As a reduction of revenue'. Choices are shuffled per session (src/lib/random.ts:43), so 'either way' has no fixed referent. ASC 740-10-45-25 ties the alternatives to interest expense (for interest) and to another expense classification (for penalties), not to 'operating expense' generally.
fix: Key: 'As income tax expense, or as interest expense (interest) and another expense line (penalties), by an accounting policy election applied consistently and disclosed.' Distractors: 'Only as income tax expense'; 'Only as interest expense, never as income tax'; 'As an adjustment to the liability for unrecognized tax benefits with no expense'. Keep the policy-election explanation.

issue: Redundancy. The same one-step facts are drilled the same way more than three times, while major ASC 740 topics get no items at all.
evidence: Clusters. (1) Noncurrent classification: far-tax-07 and far-tax-27 (0.86 stem similarity, same four options), plus flashcard fc7 and a lesson takeaway. (2) VA = DTA × % not realized: chk2, far-tax-16, far-tax-23, far-x3-07 (16 and 23 have 0.65 similarity). (3) DTA/DTL = one difference × rate: far-tax-05, -11, -21, -22, x3-18. (4) Basic current/total provision with a permanent item: far-tax-01/02, -13, -24/25, x3-08, plus all three TBS. With 28 practice MCQs, about 18 sit in these four clusters.
fix: Keep one or two items per cluster. Replace far-tax-27, far-tax-23, far-tax-21 and far-tax-25 with items on untested topics: the ASU 2023-09 rate reconciliation, intraperiod allocation with the with-and-without approach, a VA judgment from mixed evidence (cumulative losses vs. DTL reversals and tax-planning strategies), a rate change applied to a DTA with an existing VA, and a UTP that fails the recognition step.
